title: Playmats, deck boxes and sleeves
summary: The play table in TCG Card Shop Simulator is made of parts: the game keeps a set of table items, and the playmat and the deck box have meshes of their own rather than being textures on the table.
body: The play table is not simply a table. The game keeps a set of table items, and the playmat, the deck box and the cards are parts of that set rather than props that happen to be nearby.
A playmat is a mesh of its own, with a background that darkens behind it, which is why the mat reads as a surface the cards sit on rather than as a picture printed on the table.
A deck box has a mesh and a filter of its own, so it can be picked up and moved like an object while still being tied to the deck it holds.

The game ships more than one deck box design. There is artwork for a plain box, more than one numbered box, a nine-up tower box and a six-up penny-sleeve box, so the size of the box you use is a choice rather than a fixed part of the table.

Sleeves are themed. The game ships sleeve artwork for wind, fire and earth, one for its own set, and a second plain design, which is why the same deck can look different at the table from how it looks in the binder.
The game ships dice artwork as well, so what sits on the table is not limited to cards and boxes.
The images beside this entry are the game's own: a deck box texture carrying the game's own branding, and the pictures the game uses for an empty playmat slot and for an empty deck box.
The dice are pictured as well: the icon the game draws for them sits beside this entry, so what goes on the table is not only cards and boxes.
What this entry does not tell you: what any of these accessories costs, how many designs exist, or whether they change how the card game plays. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The play table keeps its own set of items, with the playmat, the deck box and the cards as parts of it.
A playmat has a mesh of its own and a background that darkens behind it.
A deck box has a mesh and a filter of its own.
The game ships artwork for more than one deck box, including a nine-up tower box and a six-up penny-sleeve box.
facts.evidence: asset names: T_DeckBox, T_DeckBox4, T_9_UP_TowerDeckbox, T_6_UP_PennySleeves

facts.claim: Sleeve artwork exists for wind, fire and earth, for the game's own set, and for a second plain design.
facts.evidence: asset names: T_CardSleeveWind, T_CardSleeveFire, T_CardSleeveEarth, T_CardSleeveTetramon, CardSleeve_second

facts.claim: The game ships dice artwork as well, including a texture for a dice box.
The game ships a picture for an empty playmat slot.
The game ships a picture for an empty deck box slot as well.
The game ships a dice icon for the play table.
A second dice icon is shipped in a different colour.
The game ships a tower deck box of its own as well as the flat ones.
A further deck box is shipped in the game, branded for its card game.
The sleeves a card goes into are a set of their own, with a material for them.
The build names accessories individually, including a card preserver, platinum-series pocket pages and a magnetic holder.
Further accessories are named as well: a semi-rigid card holder, a toploader, six-up penny sleeves and two more playmat designs.
facts.evidence: asset names: Icon_4_UP_SemiRigidCardHolder, Icon_5_UP_Toploader, Icon_6_UP_PennySleeves, Icon_7_UP_PlaymatB, Icon_7_UP_PlaymatC

facts.claim: The platinum-series pocket pages have a material of their own, named for the set.
The dice box is carried in a low-detail form and in a glass form beside the ordinary one.
The playmat designs run past the ones already named, and a clear sleeve is named beside the element sleeves.
facts.evidence: asset names: Icon_Playmat10, Icon_Playmat11, Icon_Playmat12, Icon_CardSleeveClear

facts.claim: The sleeve designs each have an icon of their own, one for each of the game's card elements.
facts.evidence: asset names: Icon_CardSleeveEarth, Icon_CardSleeveFire, Icon_CardSleeveWater, Icon_CardSleeveWind, Icon_CardSleeveTetramon

facts.claim: Further playmat icons are numbered beside the ones already named.
The card accessories carry their own materials as well, named per accessory.
facts.evidence: asset names: MAT_1_UP_MagneticHolder, MAT_2_UP_CardPreserver, MAT_6_UP_PennySleeves, MAT_7_UP_Playmat

sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each fact is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
